drug_class: Combined Hormonal Contraceptive (Estrogen + Progestin birth control pill)
purpose: This medication is used to prevent pregnancy. It can also be used to treat moderate acne in women who choose to use the pill for birth control, and it may help with the symptoms of premenstrual dysphoric disorder (PMDD), such as mood changes and bloating. Some forms are also used to treat symptoms of premenstrual syndrome (PMS).
how_it_works: This pill contains two hormones — estrogen and progestin — that work together to prevent pregnancy in three ways. First, they stop your ovaries from releasing an egg each month. Second, they thicken the mucus at the cervix so sperm have a harder time getting through. Third, they thin the lining of the uterus so that even if an egg were fertilized, it would have trouble implanting.
common_side_effects: Some common side effects include nausea, headaches, breast tenderness or swelling, spotting or light bleeding between periods (especially in the first few months), mood changes, and decreased sex drive. Many of these side effects improve after the first two to three months of use.
warnings: This medication is not right for everyone. You should NOT take it if you smoke and are over 35 years old, as this raises the risk of serious blood clots, stroke, or heart attack. It can also raise potassium levels in your blood, so let your doctor know if you take other medications that affect potassium. It does NOT protect against sexually transmitted infections (STIs). Tell your doctor if you have a history of blood clots, high blood pressure, migraines with aura, liver problems, or certain cancers. Stop taking it and call your doctor right away if you have chest pain, shortness of breath, sudden severe headache, vision changes, or leg pain or swelling.
typical_dosing: You take one pill by mouth every day, at the same time each day. Most packs are 28-day packs — some pills are active hormone pills and some are reminder (inactive or placebo) pills. You should take them in the exact order shown on the pack. Taking your pill at the same time every day helps it work best and can reduce side effects like nausea. If you miss a pill, follow the instructions that come with your pack or ask your pharmacist what to do.
